# TidyWL for Netflix

> Free Chrome extension that brings back Netflix's old My List page on a computer: since version 1.3.0 (October 9, 2026) it adds a "My List" link beside My Netflix in Netflix's own top menu, which opens every title on My List in one grid, the page Netflix replaced in September 2026 with a single sideways row. It also opens a dashboard over netflix.com for My List: an IMDb rating and details on every title, filters and sorting, bulk remove, search with the categories Netflix hides, and the custom playlists Netflix does not offer. No account. Since version 1.1.0 it also puts IMDb ratings on Netflix's own title cards, and since version 1.2.0 it marks the titles in My List that Netflix is about to remove. An optional subscription, TidyWL Pro for Netflix, available since version 1.0.0, adds Tonight (a pick for who is watching, the time you have and the mood), Undo, pins, clean-up rules, stats, more playlists, and playlists synced to other browsers and a phone, with a 7-day free trial since version 1.1.0.

On the Chrome Web Store it is listed as **Watch Later Tidy for Netflix: IMDb Ratings & Hidden Categories** (since version 1.2.2; before that, Watch Later Tidy for Netflix); inside the extension it is called TidyWL for Netflix. It is a separate extension from TidyWL for YouTube, by the same developer, described at [tidywl.com/llms.txt](https://tidywl.com/llms.txt). Nothing about the YouTube extension applies to this one: not its features, its browsers, its prices, its Pro or its privacy policy.

## What it does

On netflix.com, press Alt+L (Option+L on a Mac), or open it from the toolbar button's popup, and a dashboard opens over the page with three tabs. Sync reads the active profile's My List and watch state once and keeps them in the browser; opening the dashboard after that asks Netflix for nothing. In every tab, resting the pointer on a title's picture opens Netflix's own preview (since version 1.3.0), with Play, add or remove from My List, rate and more info, and the synopsis, cast, director or creators, and genres added under it; if Netflix's preview cannot open, the dashboard's own panel shows those details instead. A pinned title cannot be removed from the preview, and more info opens Netflix's full view of the title over the dashboard.

- **My List** — every title as a card with its year, runtime (films) or seasons (shows), maturity rating, genres and IMDb rating. One Filter menu narrows by type, availability (including Leaving soon, since version 1.2.0), watch state (watched, partway, not started, for films and shows), IMDb rating, runtime, and pinned or not. A breakdown of the list by genre, biggest first, filters by genre in one click, as does each card's genre. Sort by IMDb rating, runtime, year or title, or group by type, watch state or decade. Bulk remove: tick as many titles as you like, review the exact list, and remove them in one run. Export the whole list, the ticked titles or what is filtered, as CSV or JSON, with the date the extension first saw each title, which Netflix does not show. Since version 0.2.0 a JSON export, from another browser or profile, can be imported into My List with a button or by dropping the file on the dashboard.
- **Search and browse** — search Netflix's catalogue by title, actor or director, and browse more than a hundred categories Netflix keeps out of its own genre picker (which ones appear varies by region). A category sorts A–Z, Z–A, by year or in Netflix's suggested order, which Netflix's own website stopped offering in May 2026, or by IMDb rating. Since version 1.0.0 each result also carries its year, runtime or seasons, maturity rating and IMDb rating, read in behind a progress bar that can be stopped, so results can be filtered and sorted too. Add any title to My List, one at a time or in bulk, or straight into a playlist without adding it to My List.
- **IMDb ratings on Netflix itself** (since version 1.1.0, free) — on the home page, in search and in every category, each title's art carries its IMDb rating in the top-right corner; a click opens the title on IMDb. The trailer at the top of the home page carries one too, or a "?" that says why there is none. A title with fewer than 100 votes gets none. The badges ask Netflix nothing: the title id is in each card's link.
- **The My List page, back** (since version 1.3.0, free) — a "My List" link beside My Netflix in Netflix's own top menu opens every title in My List as a grid of cards, in Netflix's order, the way the page looked before Netflix folded it into one row of My Netflix. Hovering a card opens Netflix's own preview; clicking it opens the title. The cards carry the IMDb rating badges and, for a title the last Sync found leaving, a Leaving soon label. A title removed there leaves the grid at once, and Netflix's Undo brings it back. A button opens the dashboard. The page reads the list from Netflix each time it opens, so no Sync is needed, and stores nothing. The link is named in the profile's language in English, German, Spanish, French, Japanese, Brazilian Portuguese and Chinese, and in English otherwise.
- **Leaving soon** (since version 1.2.0, free) — Sync marks each title in My List that Netflix is about to remove, with Netflix's own sentence about its last day, shown as Netflix wrote it. A filter shows only those titles, in My List and in playlists, and every count says which Sync it comes from, since Netflix's list changes daily. The toolbar button's popup lists them with their pictures, and its badge counts the titles that started leaving since the popup was last opened. It asks Netflix once per 100 titles, and only when Sync is pressed.
- **Playlists** — custom playlists, which Netflix does not offer at all. Copy titles in from My List, from search or from another playlist; Move also takes them out of My List, or out of the playlist they came from. Reorder a playlist by dragging or with Move to top and Move to bottom, and filter it by type, availability, watch state, IMDb rating and runtime. Playlists belong to the Netflix profile they were made on, are never written to the Netflix account, and are carried between the user's own signed-in Chrome browsers by Chrome's own sync. They can be exported to a file and imported in another browser.

## Playlist limits

- **Free:** up to five playlists, counted across all the Netflix profiles in that browser (since version 1.0.0).
- **A browser that had the extension before version 1.0.0** keeps making up to 50 per profile without Pro.
- **With Pro:** up to 50 per profile.
- **Every playlist** holds up to 500 titles.

The five is checked only when a new playlist is made. Nothing is taken away: a browser already past five, or a subscription that lapses, keeps every playlist it has.

## TidyWL Pro for Netflix

A paid subscription, available since version 1.0.0. It is separate from TidyWL Pro for YouTube and has its own keys: a key for one does not work in the other. Everything above is free; Pro adds:

- **Tonight** (since version 1.1.0) — choose who is watching (just you, a partner, friends or family), how long you have (short, a movie, or any length) and a mood, or tap a saved night, and it deals one pick and two backups from My List, each with its reason: IMDb rating, runtime, the genre that fits. With family leaves out anything rated above the youngest viewer. Re-roll deals more; "Not tonight" hides a pick for seven days, and a title put off three times in 30 days is marked in My List. Surprises from outside My List that fit the mood are included unless switched off. It leaves out what the profile has finished and anything it gave a thumbs down, read from its Netflix viewing history and thumbs. "Later, on my phone" keeps the pick at the top of the TidyWL phone app until 5 am. Alt+T opens it on any Netflix page, as does a "Pick for me" button in the corner of Netflix's pages. Since version 1.2.0 a title Netflix is about to remove gets a small nudge in Tonight and says so, and the dashboard names a title in My List when it starts leaving.
- **Undo** — titles removed from My List through the extension are kept for 90 days on that device and can be put back.
- **Pin** — a pinned title cannot be removed by a clean-up rule, a Move or a bulk remove. Unpinning never needs Pro, and a pin already made keeps protecting its title whatever the plan.
- **Two clean-up rules** — move what has been watched into a "Watched" playlist, and titles never started that have waited six months into a "Someday" playlist. Each shows the list before anything moves.
- **Stats** — hours of film still waiting, and titles added against titles watched, month by month.
- **Up to 50 playlists per profile.**
- **Mobile sync** — playlists kept in step through tidywl.com across browsers Chrome's own sync does not reach, such as Brave or another Google account, and readable on a phone at tidywl.com/netflix/app after pairing it once with a code from the extension; the phone shows every synced profile's playlists, a tap to switch. The phone is read-only.
- **Feature requests and support answered first.**

Undo, pins, the rules, stats and Tonight run in the browser. Pro starts with a 7-day free trial, card required, since version 1.1.0: nothing is charged until the trial ends, and cancelling before then costs nothing. After checkout, Pro switches itself on in that browser; a key can also be pasted in the dashboard, or found again from any Paddle receipt. Pro is a key, not an account: no password, and Paddle takes the payment, so the buyer's card and email never reach TidyWL. Prices, refunds and terms are on the [pricing page](https://tidywl.com/netflix/pricing/).

## Privacy

- **Stays in the browser:** My List, watch state, which titles are leaving (since version 1.2.0), searches, removal history and stats — and, with Pro since version 1.1.0, the viewing history and thumbs Tonight reads from Netflix (title ids, last-play times and thumbs only), so it never offers what the viewer has seen or disliked. Playlists and pins travel between the user's signed-in Chrome browsers through Chrome's own sync, which goes to Google, not to TidyWL.
- **Pro sync, only when switched on:** that profile's playlists, with each title's name, type, year and picture link, and the profile's name, go to tidywl.com so other browsers and the phone can show them; so does the one pick sent with Tonight's "Later, on my phone", gone at 5 am. A Pro key goes to tidywl.com to be checked, and never reaches the phone.
- **A usage report, from version 0.2.0:** a random install id and lifetime counts (titles removed and added, searches run, categories opened, playlists made, days opened, days the rating badges showed (since version 1.2.2), My List size, how often Pro's offer was shown, Tonight's plays and re-rolls, and the like; the privacy policy lists every one) to tidywl.com, only when a count has changed. Never a title, a search term, a category or a profile. There is no switch to turn it off in the extension; uninstalling stops it.
- **When it is removed, since version 1.2.1:** Chrome opens one page on tidywl.com asking why. Its address carries the version, the browser's language, roughly how long the extension was installed and on how many days its dashboard was opened; none of it reaches tidywl.com unless the person answers and presses Send. An email is asked for only after that, is optional, and is deleted after 60 days.
- **Five other requests, none identifying an install:** a public settings file from tidywl.com; IMDb's public daily ratings dataset; Netflix's numeric title ids sent to Wikidata to match them to IMDb ids; a title's name sent to IMDb's search and Wikidata's when its id cannot be matched; and, since version 1.1.0, the numeric ids of the Netflix titles on screen sent to tidywl.com's ratings table for the badges.
- **What it does not do:** it never asks for a Netflix password and never touches, downloads or records video. It runs on netflix.com, and on the one tidywl.com page shown after checkout, to switch Pro on; nowhere else.

Every request and every stored key is listed in the [privacy policy](https://tidywl.com/netflix/privacy/).

## Seeing the whole My List after Netflix's September 2026 change

Around September 15, 2026, Netflix's website replaced the My List page with **My Netflix** (`netflix.com/browse/my-list`), where My List is one row you scroll sideways, between Continue Watching and Trailers You've Watched. Netflix offers no known way to switch back. On a computer, this extension shows the whole list at once, in two ways. Since version 1.3.0 it puts the page itself back: a "My List" link beside My Netflix in Netflix's top menu opens every title in one grid, in Netflix's order, with Netflix's own preview on hover (checked live on 2026-10-08, a 653-title list). And on any Netflix page, Alt+L opens the dashboard, whose My List tab shows every title as a card with filters, sorting and the titles leaving soon (checked live on 2026-10-06, a 160-title list). Both are free and run in Chrome on a computer only.

- [How to get Netflix's old My List page back](https://tidywl.com/netflix/blog/see-your-whole-netflix-my-list/): the steps, with screenshots of the My List page and the dashboard
- [What happened to Netflix's My List page](https://tidywl.com/netflix/blog/what-happened-to-netflix-my-list/): what changed, why people are unhappy, and the options

## Requirements

- Chrome on a computer. Chrome for Android has no extension support; with Pro, playlists can be read on a phone.
- A Netflix subscription and a signed-in netflix.com session. It works through that session.
- Published on the Chrome Web Store since 2026-09-21.
